thread:
alex: Heads up — CI artifact from yesterday's build (s3://redwood-ci/artifacts/2026-03-18.zip) contains a file `deploy/old_tokens.txt` with what looks like a set of legacy API keys. I pulled a quick grep: `grep -E \"rwinf_[A-Za-z0-9]{32}\" deploy/old_tokens.txt` and got multiple matches.
maria: ugh. how did that end up in the artifact? which job created it?
jamal: it appears the legacy creds were generated for a migration in 2023 and accidentally left in a temp dir. job `ci-deploy` archives `deploy/` without filtering.
security-oncall: (automated) Incident ticket created: SEC-2026-317. Severity: P2. Recommended immediate actions: revoke affected tokens, block usage, and audit access logs.
alex: I'll start revocation now. @jamal can you confirm which env/service these keys map to? if they're customer-facing we need notif.
jamal: quick mapping shows three tokens tied to service-account `svc-ingest-legacy` and two tied to an internal analytics pipeline. No public client keys.
nina: I'll run a CloudTrail/Access Log search for token usage from last 6 months and filter for the token fingerprints. If any external IPs used them, escalate.
maria: Steps we should do now: 1) Revoke/rotate tokens. 2) Block any active sessions. 3) Check S3 ACLs & artifact publishing job. 4) Notify legal if customer data could be impacted. 5) Patch CI to remove archiving of sensitive paths.
jamal: revoking tokens now -> `terraform apply -target=redwood_token.revocation["svc-ingest-legacy"]` (running). tagging tickets with rotation commit hash.
security-oncall: Confirmed: revoke requests submitted. Also recommend immediate KMS rewrap for service keys and enforce RBAC so CI runner cannot read plain tokens.
alex: @maria can you patch the pipeline to add exclusion for `deploy/*.txt` and add a secret-scan step? keep it minimal, then we'll revert later if needed.
maria: on it. adding `--exclude deploy/*.txt` to the archive step and enabling `truffleHog` scan. will open a PR.
jamal: found two token usages in CloudTrail from internal IPs only, last use 2025-11-02. No sign of exfiltration to external IPs so far. adding additional query for suspicious S3 GETs.
nina: audit logs pulled — no anomalies in egress patterns. I cross-referenced with known compromised IP lists. so far clean. saving results to SEC-2026-317 for postmortem.
legal: preliminary input — if these are internal-only tokens and no customer data accessed, low regulatory exposure. keep me in loop if any customer-facing tokens show activity.
alex: action items captured: revoke tokens (done), patch CI (maria), add secret-scan + denylist (jamal), run org-wide artifact scan for similar files (nina), enforce KMS for all service credentials and add RBAC change to prevent token persistence in workspace (security-oncall).
jamal: added an org-wide S3 bucket scan job: `aws s3api list-objects --bucket redwood-ci --prefix artifacts/ --query 'Contents[].Key' | xargs -n1 aws s3 cp s3://redwood-ci/{} - | grep -E \"rwinf_[A-Za-z0-9]{32}\"` — running across last 90 days.
maria: PR: https://github.com/redwood/ci/pull/812 — excludes deploy text files + adds trufflehog run. please review.
security-oncall: Monitoring rule created: alert if any token that matches legacy pattern is used in production logs. Also added audit log retention snapshot for the next 90 days.
alex: any customer impact? jamal said internal-only but double-check any downstream ingest that might have forwarded data.
jamal: checked ingest logs — none of the legacy tokens were used to accept customer payloads. they're tied to orchestration jobs only.
nina: final check on S3 public exposures: bucket ACLs are private; last public object event none.
legal: recommend customer comms not necessary. we'll re-evaluate if new info emerges.
alex: good. let's do a short postmortem template: timeline, root cause (CI archived temp file), remediation (revoked tokens, CI patch, secret-scan, KMS/RBAC), follow-ups (enforce pre-commit hook, org artifact retention policy). assign owners.
maria: I'll draft the postmortem and link SEC-2026-317 and the PR.
jamal: will add RBAC change PR to remove token creation permissions from legacy service accounts and require KMS for new keys.
security-oncall: Closing immediate incident phase. Transitioning to remediation backlog items. If anyone finds unexpected activity, re-open SEC-2026-317. :thumbsup:
alex: thanks everyone. quick wins done, major follow-ups in backlog. appreciate the fast responses.
